subject: Performance gating: reserved GPU shortlist & mutual signoff
messages:

Date: Mon, 25 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance gating: reserved GPU shortlist & mutual signoff

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the pilot: 

High-level ask from Novaforge: sustained P95 latency target of <= 180ms for 4k-context generation (streaming enabled), expected steady-state throughput ~110 qps with short bursts to 220 qps, and ~18 concurrent streaming sessions.

What we observed in the demo and what we recommend for the dedicated validation pilot:
- Target SLOs to gate on during pilot: P95 <= 180ms, tail behavior analysis to 99th percentile, cold-start 1st-token latency under 240ms.
- Pilot throughput window: sustained 100–120 qps for 48 hours to stress autoscaler + KV cache hit-rate tracking.
- Concurrency profile: 12–20 active streaming sessions; we will instrument per-session KV retention and eviction behavior.

Reserved GPU shortlist (tradeoffs + ask for signoff):
1) NVIDIA H100 80GB (recommended for latency headroom) — pros: best single-stream latency at high context lengths, strong bfloat16 throughput; cons: higher hourly cost, limited availability in some regions.
2) NVIDIA A100 80GB (balanced option) — pros: predictable throughput and good memory for long contexts; cons: slightly higher P95 at 4k vs H100 for some models.
3) NVIDIA L40s (cost-optimized for batchy workloads) — pros: cheaper and good for high throughput; cons: less headroom for low-latency streaming.

Attachments: perf_matrix_v3.xlsx (bench summary), MAP_draft.pdf (mutual action plan draft), pilot_bench_config.yaml (bench harness config).

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Please confirm which GPU(s) you want in the pilot shortlist (choose up to 2) by EOD Wed, 09/27.
- Confirm the primary decision owner on Novaforge side for performance signoff (name + email).
- We will provision a reserved pilot cluster (2 nodes) for the shortlisted GPU type(s) and run the 48-hour sustained-window test. We’ll provide: bench harness, logs + token-level tracing, and a dashboard slice for 1:1 review.

If Novaforge prefers a lower-cost pathway we can also run a quantized-LLM variant for throughput checks — will need a quick confirm of acceptable quality delta.

I’ll queue Karthik and Ben to prepare bench configs and cost delta estimates once you confirm shortlist.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational clarifications for the pilot run (bench ops owner notes):

- Bench config: we’ll run two nodes (1 control, 1 spare) with identical machine types. Pilot harness will iterate through: single-stream latency, multi-stream concurrency ramps, and sustained qps windows. The pilot_bench_config.yaml includes exact request shapes and token distributions.
- Observability: we will provide a Grafana slice with P50/P95/P99, token emission rate, KV cache hit-rate, and stream connection breakdown.
- Data handling: logs will be redacted for PII; if Novaforge wants full trace exports we’ll arrange a limited access S3 bucket with TTL 30 days.
- Cost delta: Ben please attach the rough per-hour delta for H100 vs A100 vs L40s in the pilot context.

I’ll coordinate scheduling for the 48-hour run once Alyssa confirms shortlist.
